turn_text: So from your perspective, what caused this supply chain bottleneck that we're facing now? Can Washington actually help and resolve it, or is this something that will just take time for the market and private industry to work out?

Well, the thing about it, I come from the private sector. I spent 22 years there. I was part of the supply chain caucus before we even ended up in a pandemic. And most of these supply chains are private supply chains and you're exactly right. You ask what caused it. Look, as I said, when you've got shipping containers that are sitting off ports in America for weeks and weeks and weeks, that's a problem. And so some of the shipping reform legislation that we've passed to provide some efficiency in unloading those containers, some of those container companies have taken advantage of the situation. price gouged American consumers. And when you import so much from China and China is literally shut down, you've got a huge supply chain gap in goods coming to America. So how do we fix this? The shipping reform act that we passed a couple of weeks ago, I think, was a good bill that will help. But you're exactly right. Some of this is just going to take time. I would add though that You know, on the gas and fuel side of this, I'm more of an all of the above energy kind of Democrat.
